title: Stop interpolating raw error.toString() into localized error messages across progress screens
rule: EH-5 / custom_lint no_e_to_string_in_ui (currently enforcing nothing repo-wide)
why: error.toString() on a Dart/Firebase/Drift exception is always in English (e.g. 'Bad state: ...', 'SqliteException: ...') and not ICU-pluralizable; interpolating it into an otherwise-Hebrew ARB string means a Hebrew-locale, RTL user who hits any of these error states sees a sentence that switches to raw untranslated English mid-string. recent_activity_screen.dart in the same directory shows the correct pattern (l10n.chartFailedToLoad with no error interpolation, 4 uses) — the other 4 screens in this same feature diverge from it.
recommendation: Replace error.toString() interpolation with the generic localized failure string (as recent_activity_screen.dart already does) and, if diagnostic detail is genuinely needed, log error.toString() via AppLogger instead of rendering it to the user.
acceptance_criteria: None of the 4 screens' AsyncValue.error branches call .toString() on the error object inside a Text/l10n call.
Once dart run custom_lint is repaired, no_e_to_string_in_ui reports zero hits in lib/features/progress/.

corrections: Narrative says recent_activity_screen.dart uses the correct pattern '4 uses' — actual grep shows 5 uses of l10n.chartFailedToLoad; trivial miscount, doesn't affect the finding's validity.

The corroborating claim 'recent_activity_screen.dart ... 4 uses' undercounts: grep confirms 5 uses of l10n.chartFailedToLoad with no error interpolation (lines 343, 378, 572, 628, 651). Does not affect the primary 6-site defect, which is fully accurate.
